with every consent: never what tells two accounts apart (MAG-351).

and single-use: without it, anyone could post a code to our callback.

usable.description:
Whether the bank will still answer. Expiry is checked at read time
rather than trusted from the stored status, which only a sync updates.

capital, the payment and the rate, and a fourth field would contradict
them at the first early repayment.

RecurringOperation.description:
A series the owner expects to see again — rent on the 5th, Netflix on the
12th. Abstract: its occurrences are computed by `RecurrenceSchedule`, never
written down, and the real transactions stay what they are.

It recognises its transactions through the engine the categorization rules
use, with the expected counterparty as the main criterion.

counterpartyName.description: The payee of an expense, the payer of an income: who the bank names.

counterpartyKey.description: Derived from the name, like a transaction's, so the two compare.

labelPattern.description: Read in the label when there is no counterparty to compare.

category.description: The default category, inherited by the transactions attached to it.

account.description: Its currency is the operation's: there is no other.

anchorOn.description: Where the series is counted from, never from the previous occurrence.

referenceAmountCents.description: Signed cents: negative is an expense, positive an income.

endsOn.description: The last day an occurrence may fall on; null while the series runs.

monthlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a month, in cents.

yearlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a year, in cents.

SafetyCushion.description:
The safety net, configured once per user. Its current amount is never
stored here — it is the balance of the accounts flagged as cushion.

targetMonths.description: How many months of net income the cushion should hold.

monthlyNetIncomeCents.description: Reference monthly net income, in cents.

rechargeCapCents.description: Most that may be put back into the cushion per month, in cents.

rechargeTargetMonths.description: Months the user would like a recharge to take, before the cap applies.

completedAt.description: First time the target was ever reached — tells building from recharging.

targetCents.description: The amount the cushion should hold, in cents.

amountCents.description: Signed amount in integer cents: negative = expense/debit, positive = income/credit.

counterpartyName.description:
Who the money came from or went to, kept apart from the label: the bank
rewrites the label every month, never the creditor. Not the same thing
as `counterpart`, the opposite leg of an internal transfer.

externalId.description:
The bank's own reference for the movement (`entry_reference`), when it
gives one: the same movement read twice, whatever its label became.

counterpartyKey.description: The name folded so two spellings of one payee group together.

retrospect.description: What the user made of this spend at the monthly review.

categorySource.description: How the category was set: by hand, by a rule, or not at all.

transferKind.description:
What kind of neutral movement this is — an internal transfer, a rejected
payment — if any. Anything but `None` is neither an expense nor an
income, and leaves every aggregate.

transferSource.description: Who decided it: the detection, or the user by hand.

counterpart.description:
The other leg of the same movement. Null when only one of the two
accounts is known — the normal case when a single bank is synced.

recurringOperation.description:
The recurring operation this line is one occurrence of. Written over
REST by a PATCH that names it with `recurringOccurrenceOn`, which the
processor turns into a manual attachment: the setters below only exist
for the deserializer, the domain goes through `attachToRecurring()`.

recurringOccurrenceOn.description: The due date of the occurrence this line settles, not its booking day.

recurringSource.description: Who attached or detached it: the automatic attachment leaves `manual` alone for good.
